answer: Sybil resistance works by making each identity carry real, slashable capital: an agent must bond a stake backed by a hardware key before it can transact, one agent to one bond. Faking a thousand personas means locking collateral a thousand times and exposing every clone to forfeiture once peers prove misbehaviour, so the cost of the quill grows with each fake name. Honest nodes verify signatures against that stake at the wharf of settlement, and a beacon of attested history makes untested clones stand out. Cost scales linearly for attackers, once for honest agents.
